name: Limited Use Motorcycle
description: A moped: a motor vehicle with two or three wheels and a seat or saddle whose maximum performance speed is 40 mph or less, in class A (over 30 to 40 mph), class B (over 20 to 30 mph) or class C (20 mph or less). An electric moped qualifies by its top speed, and an e-bike past the bicycle with electric assist limits lands here when it has a seat and tops out at 40 mph.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels and a seat or saddle for the operator, with a maximum performance speed of 40 mph or less; there's no pedal, engine-size or power requirement, so an electric moped qualifies by its top speed
Class A tops out over 30 mph up to 40 mph, class B over 20 mph up to 30 mph, and class C at 20 mph or less
Only a model its manufacturer has certified as a limited use motorcycle can be registered
Registered with the DMV, every class; no title required
A New York dealer must register it at the time of sale unless the buyer signs a declaration that it's for use only outside the state
restrictions.citation: Vehicle and Traffic Law §2261, as amended by S7703-B (chapter 198 of 2024)

restrictions.rule: Class A riders need a motorcycle license (class M or MJ); class B and class C riders need a driver's license of any class
Liability insurance required for class A and class B, and for a class C used as a rental
Class A and class B riders must wear a helmet
Class A may use any traffic lane; class B and class C stay in the right-hand lane or on the shoulder except to turn left
Class A needs a safety inspection

In New York City, one that can't be registered with the DMV is a motorized scooter, which can't be ridden on streets, in parks or in other public places: a $250 civil penalty, and impound when it's ridden in a way that endangers anyone
In New York City, selling, leasing or renting one that can't be registered carries a $1,000 civil penalty, $2,000 for each further one within a year, and the device can be impounded
